title: Employee Wage Accounts — Create / Edit
overviewHtml:
Which ledger account one of the employee's wage types posts to, from a given date, and under which cost elements. The cost engine and the journal voucher exports read these to post the employee's pay.

Records for the same employee and wage type form a history: saving a new one closes the previous one on the day before the new start date. A wage type can be split across several accounts starting on the same date, as long as the percentages add up to no more than 100.

fields.label: WageTypeId
fields.rules: Required. Chosen from Wage Type master data.
fields.html:
What it is. The wage type this mapping is for.

Example. Housing Allowance
fields.adminHtml: Maintained under Payroll Management → Wage Types. Only wage types included in FI posting are posted.

fields.label: StartDate
fields.rules: Required. Date value. Saving closes the previous record for the same employee and wage type on the day before this date; the latest record stays open.
fields.html: What it is. The first day this record applies.

fields.label: CostPercentage
fields.html:
What it is. The share of this wage type's amount posted to this account.

Example. 100

Why it matters. The cost engine posts this percentage of the wage type's total. Records for the same employee, wage type and start date cannot add up to more than 100.

fields.label: AccountInfoId
fields.rules: Required. Chosen from Account Info master data.
fields.html:
What it is. The ledger account the amount is posted to.

Example. 510100 — Salaries and Wages

fields.label: OffsetAccountInfoId
fields.rules: Optional. Chosen from Account Info master data.
fields.html:
What it is. The balancing account for the journal entry.

Example. 210500 — Salaries Payable

Why it matters. When set, the journal voucher posts the other side of the entry to this account.

fields.label: MergeOffsetAccount
fields.html:
What it is. Whether offset lines to the same account are combined into one line in the journal voucher.

Why it matters. Read when the journal voucher is built.

fields.label: CostElement1Id
fields.rules: Optional. Chosen from Cost Element master data.
fields.html:
What it is. Cost element 1 — one of up to seven accounting dimensions.

Why it matters. The cost engine copies it onto the employee's cost register lines, and the journal voucher export prints its code. Offset lines merge only when all seven cost elements match.
